rows.label: Risumlund 2026
rows.population: 1–3 CRLM, each ≤4 cm and suitable for both treatments; 100 randomized, 92 modified ITT.
rows.result: 1-year freedom from local progression: MWA 77.7% versus SBRT 83.0%; HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.43–1.74), p=0.70. Grade ≥2 toxicity 25% versus 3%.
rows.caution: No demonstrated local-control difference; wide CI and postrandomization exclusions. No survival/noninferiority claim. Grade ≥3 toxicity occurred only after MWA, including one treatment-related death.
rows.summary: One-year freedom from local progression 77.7% vs 83.0%; HR 0.87 (0.43–1.74), p=0.70.
rows.shortCaution: Small randomized study; no equivalence claim. Grade ≥2 toxicity 25% vs 3%.
rows.author: Risumlund

rows.label: SABR-COMET LT

rows.population: Thermal ablation vs resection (CRLM, one to ten lesions ≤3 cm)

rows.author: van der Lei

rows.label: Mokkarala 2019
rows.population: 202 CRLM patients; 44 matched pairs, DEB-TACE versus TARE.
rows.result: Adjusted OS association for DEB-TACE: HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.54–1.65), p=0.83; toxicity trend 27% versus 9.1%, p=0.057.
rows.caution: No significant survival difference; baseline burden and extrahepatic disease varied. Not an equivalence trial.
rows.summary: OS HR 0.94 (0.54–1.65); toxicity 27% vs 9.1%, not significant.
rows.shortCaution: Retrospective; limited precision and no equivalence inference.
rows.author: Mokkarala

rows.label: Fiorentini RCT (n=74)
rows.population: DEBIRI (irinotecan-bead chemoembolization) vs FOLFIRI
rows.result: Primary endpoint met: median OS 22 vs 15 mo (P = .031); median PFS 7 vs 4 mo (P = .006); hepatic response 68.6% vs 20%
rows.summary: Primary endpoint met: median OS 22 vs 15 mo (P = .031); median PFS 7 vs 4 mo (P = .006); hepatic response 68.6% vs 20%

rows.shortCaution: 74 patients at two centres, open label; obsolete FOLFIRI comparator capped at four months; not reproduced
rows.author: Fiorentini

rows.label: CALGB 9481
rows.population: HAI floxuridine/dexamethasone vs bolus fluorouracil/leucovorin
rows.result: Primary endpoint met: median OS 24.4 vs 20.0 mo (P = .0034); 2-y OS 51% vs 35%; hepatic response 47% vs 24%; overall TTP no different
rows.summary: Primary endpoint met: median OS 24.4 vs 20.0 mo (P = .0034); 2-y OS 51% vs 35%; hepatic response 47% vs 24%; overall TTP no different
rows.caution: Superseded bolus comparator; no power calculation; bilirubin >3 mg/dL in 18.6% with HAI
rows.shortCaution: Superseded bolus comparator; no power calculation; bilirubin >3 mg/dL in 18.6% with HAI
rows.author: Kemeny

rows.label: Dhir 2018
rows.population: 97 pretreated liver-only CRLM patients: HAI 48 versus Y90 49, with modern systemic therapy.
rows.result: Median OS from isolated unresectable diagnosis: 31.2 versus 16.3 months (p<0.001). From initial stage IV diagnosis: 34.4 versus 32.0 months (p=0.291).
rows.caution: Retrospective, 97 patients. Survival time origin changes the apparent comparison; treatment timing, subsequent therapy and selection limit causal interpretation.
rows.summary: OS from isolated unresectable diagnosis 31.2 vs 16.3 mo; from initial stage IV diagnosis 34.4 vs 32.0 mo.
rows.shortCaution: Time origin changes interpretation; retrospective treatment selection and later therapy confound comparison.
rows.author: Dhir

rows.label: Saadat 2025
rows.population: 708 HAI versus 481 TARE patients; matched within prior systemic-therapy lines.
rows.result: TARE-versus-HAI mortality HR: 1 prior line 1.46 (95% CI 1.02–2.08); 2 lines 1.96 (1.32–2.89); 3–4 lines 0.88 (0.57–1.35).
rows.caution: HAI came from one high-volume center, TARE from five others. More subsequent systemic therapy/resection after HAI; treatment and center effects cannot be separated. Not a comparison with ablation.
rows.summary: Y90 vs HAI mortality HR 1.46 after one prior line, 1.96 after two; 0.88 after three/four.
rows.shortCaution: Nonrandom center comparison; later systemic therapy and resection differed. No ablation comparator.
rows.author: Saadat

rows.label: Boilève 2026
rows.population: Persistently unresectable liver-only CRLM after systemic induction; 11 HAI-oxaliplatin plus systemic versus 9 systemic alone randomized.
rows.result: Conversion to resection/ablation 7/11 (64%) versus 2/9 (22%), p=0.09; PFS 12.6 versus 4.37 months.
rows.caution: Very small, early-closed trial; conversion endpoint not significant. Supports further study, not a confirmed conversion advantage or direct comparison against ablation.
rows.summary: Conversion 7/11 vs 2/9 (p=0.09); median PFS 12.6 vs 4.37 mo.
rows.shortCaution: Very small randomized trial; early closure. Not a comparison with ablation.
rows.author: Boilève

rows.label: CLOCC RCT
rows.population: RFA ± resection + systemic therapy vs systemic therapy alone
rows.result: Randomised phase II; OS (secondary endpoint) HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.38-0.88), p=0.01; 8-y OS 35.9% vs 8.9%; 5-y hepatic progression 62.1% vs 88.2%
rows.summary: Randomised phase II; OS (secondary endpoint) HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.38-0.88), p=0.01; 8-y OS 35.9% vs 8.9%; 5-y hepatic progression 62.1% vs 88.2%
rows.caution: Closed early at 119 patients; survival not the primary endpoint; curves overlap for first 3 years
rows.shortCaution: Closed early at 119 patients; survival not the primary endpoint; curves overlap for first 3 years
rows.author: Ruers

rows.label: FOXFIRE/SIRFLOX/-Global
rows.population: FOLFOX + SIRT (Y-90) vs FOLFOX alone · pooled three RCTs, 1103 pts
rows.result: Primary endpoint not met: median OS 22.6 vs 23.3 mo (HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.90-1.19, p=0.61); PFS 11.0 vs 10.3 mo (NS); resection 17% vs 16%
rows.summary: Primary endpoint not met: median OS 22.6 vs 23.3 mo (HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.90-1.19, p=0.61); PFS 11.0 vs 10.3 mo (NS); resection 17% vs 16%
rows.caution: Control arm got more full-dose oxaliplatin and bevacizumab; 12% crossover; right-sided signal post hoc (179)
rows.shortCaution: Control arm got more full-dose oxaliplatin and bevacizumab; 12% crossover; right-sided signal post hoc (179)
rows.author: Wasan

rows.comparison: Y90 + arterial FUDR vs arterial FUDR
rows.label: Gray 2001
rows.population: 74 patients with bilobar unresectable CRLM: Y90 plus regional FUDR versus regional FUDR alone.
rows.result: Tumor-volume response 50% versus 24% (p=0.03); liver progression was delayed.
rows.caution: Tests adding Y90 to HAI, not Y90 versus HAI alone. Older chemotherapy era; no established overall-survival benefit. Not evidence against ablation of small lesions.
rows.summary: Tumor-volume response 50% vs 24%; delayed liver progression.
rows.shortCaution: Add-on study using older treatment; no proven OS benefit or standalone HAI–Y90 ranking.
rows.author: Gray

rows.label: Hendlisz ph III
rows.population: Y-90 + fluorouracil vs fluorouracil alone
rows.result: Primary endpoint met: median time to liver progression 5.5 vs 2.1 mo (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.20-0.72); OS 10.0 vs 7.3 mo (HR 0.92), not significant
rows.summary: Primary endpoint met: median time to liver progression 5.5 vs 2.1 mo (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.20-0.72); OS 10.0 vs 7.3 mo (HR 0.92), not significant
rows.caution: Stopped at 46 of 58 planned; 10 controls crossed over to Y-90; liver-only surrogate endpoint
rows.shortCaution: Stopped at 46 of 58 planned; 10 controls crossed over to Y-90; liver-only surrogate endpoint
rows.author: Hendlisz

rows.label: EPOCH ph III
rows.population: Y-90 + second-line chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone
rows.result: Co-primary endpoints met: PFS 8.0 vs 7.2 mo (HR 0.69), hepatic PFS 9.1 vs 7.2 mo (HR 0.59); OS 14.0 vs 14.4 mo (HR 1.07), no benefit
rows.summary: Co-primary endpoints met: PFS 8.0 vs 7.2 mo (HR 0.69), hepatic PFS 9.1 vs 7.2 mo (HR 0.59); OS 14.0 vs 14.4 mo (HR 1.07), no benefit
rows.caution: Grade ≥3 toxicity 68.4% vs 49.3%; one-sided tests; censoring at subsequent therapy; sponsor co-analysed
rows.shortCaution: Grade ≥3 toxicity 68.4% vs 49.3%; one-sided tests; censoring at subsequent therapy; sponsor co-analysed
rows.author: Mulcahy

rows.comparison: Adjuvant pump HAI vs no pump HAI
rows.label: Dutch PUMP, ASCO 2026 LBA3506
rows.population: Adjuvant after resection: expert-center discussion. Dutch PUMP did not establish PFS benefit in its low-risk population; pump FUDR is distinct from pCCA catheter therapy.
rows.result: PFS HR 0.88 (0.62–1.25), P=.48; no adjuvant systemic therapy; OS immature. DOI 10.1200/JCO.2026.44.17_suppl.LBA3506
rows.summary: PFS HR 0.88 (0.62–1.25), P=.48; no adjuvant systemic therapy; OS immature. DOI 10.1200/JCO.2026.44.17_suppl.LBA3506
rows.caution: Conference abstract; interpret within the reported trial population.
rows.shortCaution: Conference results; primary report status is shown with the source.

rows.label: Gelli 2026
rows.population: 99 patients after resection/ablation of ≥4 CRLM: HAI-oxaliplatin 50 versus IV oxaliplatin 49, both with IV LV5FU2.
rows.result: Hepatic RFS 25 versus 12 months, HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.40–0.99); OS HR 0.61 (0.33–1.12), not significant. Grade 3–4 AEs 58% versus 32%.
rows.caution: Selected adjuvant setting after complete local treatment of ≥4 CRLM. Phase II design amended before database lock; early closure and immature OS limit certainty. Oxaliplatin infusion is not FUDR pump therapy.
rows.summary: Hepatic RFS 25 vs 12 mo, HR 0.63; OS HR 0.61 (0.33–1.12).
rows.shortCaution: Adjuvant phase II; amended design. More grade 3/4 toxicity; no confirmed OS benefit.
rows.author: Gelli

rows.label: Kemeny NEJM RCT
rows.population: HAI floxuridine + systemic FU vs systemic FU alone
rows.result: Primary two-year OS 86% vs 72% (P=0.03, landmark) but whole KM curves NS (p=0.21); two-year hepatic PFS 90% vs 60% (P<0.001)
rows.summary: Primary two-year OS 86% vs 72% (P=0.03, landmark) but whole KM curves NS (p=0.21); two-year hepatic PFS 90% vs 60% (P<0.001)
rows.caution: Only 26% got more than half the planned floxuridine; 6 of 74 never received HAI; single centre
rows.shortCaution: Only 26% got more than half the planned floxuridine; 6 of 74 never received HAI; single centre
rows.author: Kemeny

rows.label: Wang 2025
rows.population: 92 randomized after CRLM surgery; modified ITT 77, HAI-FUDR plus systemic 38 versus systemic 39.
rows.result: 3-year RFS 31.4% versus 34.4%, p=0.28.
rows.caution: Stopped for FUDR supply shortage; primary endpoint negative. Exploratory early-RFS/subgroup signals do not establish routine postoperative HAI.
rows.summary: Three-year RFS 31.4% vs 34.4% (p=0.28).
rows.shortCaution: Primary endpoint negative; trial stopped for FUDR shortage; modified intention-to-treat analysis.
rows.author: Wang

rows.label: Groot Koerkamp
rows.population: Perioperative HAI vs no HAI after CRLM resection (retrospective)
rows.result: Median OS 67 vs 44 mo (P < .001); propensity-adjusted HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.59-0.76); 10-year OS 38.0% vs 23.8%
rows.summary: Median OS 67 vs 44 mo (P < .001); propensity-adjusted HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.59-0.76); 10-year OS 38.0% vs 23.8%
rows.caution: Single-centre, non-randomised over 21 years; propensity model not shown; benefit largest in low-risk patients
rows.shortCaution: Single-centre, non-randomised over 21 years; propensity model not shown; benefit largest in low-risk patients
rows.author: Groot Koerkamp

rows.label: Chen RCT
rows.population: Percutaneous ablation vs resection (solitary HCC ≤5 cm)
rows.result: ITT 4-yr OS 65.9% vs 64.0% and DFS 48.2% vs 51.6%; no significant difference (no HR reported)
rows.summary: ITT 4-yr OS 65.9% vs 64.0% and DFS 48.2% vs 51.6%; no significant difference (no HR reported)
rows.caution: 19 of 90 ablation patients withdrew and had resection; powered on 2-year recurrence, not survival
rows.shortCaution: 19 of 90 ablation patients withdrew and had resection; powered on 2-year recurrence, not survival
rows.author: Chen

rows.label: MWA vs RFA RCT
rows.population: Microwave vs radiofrequency ablation (phase 2 RCT, HCC ≤4 cm)
rows.result: 2-yr local progression 6% (6/98 lesions) vs 12% (12/104), RR 1.62 (0.66-3.94; direction unstated), P=0.27; superiority not shown; 2-yr OS 86% vs 84%
rows.summary: 2-yr local progression 6% (6/98 lesions) vs 12% (12/104), RR 1.62 (0.66-3.94; direction unstated), P=0.27; superiority not shown; 2-yr OS 86% vs 84%
rows.caution: Powered for an implausibly large difference; per-protocol, per-lesion analysis; null does not show equivalence
rows.shortCaution: Powered for an implausibly large difference; per-protocol, per-lesion analysis; null does not show equivalence
rows.author: Vietti Violi

rows.label: Xia RCT
rows.population: Repeat hepatectomy vs percutaneous RFA (recurrent HCC)
rows.result: Primary endpoint not met: 5-yr OS 43.6% vs 38.5% (HR 1.26, 95% CI 0.91-1.76, p=0.17); local repeat recurrence 21.7% vs 37.8%
rows.summary: Primary endpoint not met: 5-yr OS 43.6% vs 38.5% (HR 1.26, 95% CI 0.91-1.76, p=0.17); local repeat recurrence 21.7% vs 37.8%
rows.caution: Single-centre open-label, almost all HBV, age capped at 60; null result, not proof of equivalence
rows.shortCaution: Single-centre open-label, almost all HBV, age capped at 60; null result, not proof of equivalence
rows.author: Xia

rows.label: Ng RCT
rows.population: Resection vs radiofrequency ablation (RFA) · 218 early-stage HCC
rows.result: Resection vs RFA: recurrence 71.3% vs 81.7% (P = 0.092); 10-y OS 47.6% vs 41.8% (P = 0.531); 10-y DFS 31.9% vs 18.6% (P = 0.072); RFA not superior
rows.summary: Resection vs RFA: recurrence 71.3% vs 81.7% (P = 0.092); 10-y OS 47.6% vs 41.8% (P = 0.531); 10-y DFS 31.9% vs 18.6% (P = 0.072); RFA not superior
rows.caution: Single-centre Hong Kong RCT, mostly HBV, 2002–2007; superiority design, possibly underpowered, not equivalence
rows.shortCaution: Single-centre Hong Kong RCT, mostly HBV, 2002–2007; superiority design, possibly underpowered, not equivalence
rows.author: Ng

rows.label: SURF RCT
rows.population: Surgery vs RFA
rows.result: HCC ≤3 cm, ≤3 nodules: median RFS 3.46 vs 3.04 y (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.67-1.25; P=0.58); local recurrence 15.0% vs 28.0% of recurrences (P=0.07)
rows.summary: HCC ≤3 cm, ≤3 nodules: median RFS 3.46 vs 3.04 y (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.67-1.25; P=0.58); local recurrence 15.0% vs 28.0% of recurrences (P=0.07)
rows.caution: Stopped at 301 analysable of 600 planned (conditional power <8%); mostly solitary tumours <2 cm
rows.shortCaution: Stopped at 301 analysable of 600 planned (conditional power <8%); mostly solitary tumours <2 cm
rows.author: Takayama

rows.label: SURF final
rows.population: Surgery vs radiofrequency ablation
rows.result: Co-primary endpoints not met: 5-year OS 74.6% vs 70.4% (HR 0.96, adjusted P=0.84); 5-year RFS 42.9% vs 42.7%; local recurrence 8.0% vs 15.8%
rows.summary: Co-primary endpoints not met: 5-year OS 74.6% vs 70.4% (HR 0.96, adjusted P=0.84); 5-year RFS 42.9% vs 42.7%; local recurrence 8.0% vs 15.8%
rows.caution: Failed superiority trial (67.2% power), not proven equivalence; small solitary tumours; hard sites excluded
rows.shortCaution: Failed superiority trial (67.2% power), not proven equivalence; small solitary tumours; hard sites excluded
rows.author: Kawaguchi

rows.label: Wahl
rows.population: Single-centre retrospective · 161 RFA vs 63 SBRT patients
rows.result: better FFLP than RFA if ≥2 cm
rows.summary: better FFLP than RFA if ≥2 cm

rows.label: Xi RCT vs RFA
rows.population: SBRT vs RFA
rows.result: Recurrent HCC ≤5 cm: primary local PFS HR 0.45 (0.24–0.87); 2-y 92.7% vs 75.8%; 2–5 cm subgroup not significant; no significant PFS or OS difference
rows.summary: Recurrent HCC ≤5 cm: primary local PFS HR 0.45 (0.24–0.87); 2-y 92.7% vs 75.8%; 2–5 cm subgroup not significant; no significant PFS or OS difference
rows.caution: Composite primary endpoint counts death from any cause; single centre, open-label, no central review
rows.shortCaution: Composite primary endpoint counts death from any cause; single centre, open-label, no central review
rows.author: Xi

rows.label: Arndt 2021
rows.population: Solitary treatment-naïve HCC ≤4 cm; 68 patients, 24 matched pairs. RS versus MWA.
rows.result: Mean target-tumor PFS 57.8 versus 38.6 months (p=0.005); mean OS 59.0 versus 44.3 months (p=0.203).
rows.caution: Small matched cohorts; RS often selected for anatomy unsuitable for MWA. These are mean survival times, not medians. No proven OS superiority or equivalence.
rows.summary: Mean target PFS 57.8 vs 38.6 mo; mean OS 59.0 vs 44.3 mo, p=0.203.
rows.shortCaution: Anatomy-based selection; mean times, not medians. No proven OS superiority or equivalence.
rows.author: Arndt

rows.label: Abdalla 2026
rows.population: Solitary AJCC stage I HCC ≤4 cm; resin RS 20 versus MWA 40. RS tumors were larger.
rows.result: Main-text CR 85% versus 82.5%; adjusted PFS HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.20–1.51), OS HR 1.38 (0.30–6.34).
rows.caution: No significant PFS/OS difference. Anatomy determined treatment; deaths within 1 month excluded. Abstract CR differs from main text; main-text denominator used. No equivalence conclusion.
rows.shortCaution: RS tumors were larger; selection bias and wide CIs. Main-text CR conflicts with abstract.
rows.author: Abdalla

rows.label: Biederman 2017
rows.population: Solitary HCC ≤3 cm; RS 41 versus TACE plus MWA 80 before matching.
rows.result: After matching: no significant difference in CR (p=0.94), time to progression (p=0.83), or OS (p>0.99).
rows.caution: Comparator is TACE plus MWA, not MWA alone. Selection bias and limited power; nonsignificance does not establish equivalence.
rows.summary: No significant matched differences in complete response, progression or survival.
rows.shortCaution: Combined TACE+MWA comparator; not MWA alone or proof of equivalence.
rows.author: Biederman

rows.label: De la Garza-Ramos 2022
rows.population: Solitary HCC ≤8 cm; RS 57 versus resection 66.
rows.result: Target progression 5% versus 8%; adjusted overall-progression HR 1.16 (95% CI 0.51–2.63). Median OS not reached in either group.
rows.caution: Propensity distributions were too dissimilar to match. Different surgical candidacy and liver function prevent a claim of equivalence to resection.
rows.summary: Adjusted progression HR 1.16 (0.51–2.63); median OS unreached in both groups.
rows.shortCaution: Retrospective; inadequate overlap prevented propensity matching. Not evidence of equivalence.
rows.author: De la Garza-Ramos

rows.label: Yu 2022
rows.population: Solitary unresectable HCC ≥3 cm; TARE versus DEB-TACE plus ablation; 19 matched pairs.
rows.result: DCR 94.7% versus 100%; locoregional sessions 1.3 versus 1.9 (p=0.02). No significant survival, PFS or transplant-rate difference.
rows.caution: Combined comparator; small selected cohorts. Results do not show that TARE is superior to ablation alone.
rows.summary: Disease control 94.7% vs 100%; treatment sessions 1.3 vs 1.9.
rows.shortCaution: Retrospective; combination comparator; no significant OS/PFS difference.
rows.author: Yu

rows.comparison: LT vs non-transplant care after downstaging
rows.label: XXL RCT
rows.population: LT vs non-transplant therapy after downstaging
rows.result: 5-y OS 77.5% vs 31.2% (published HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.11–0.92); tumor-event-free survival 76.8% vs 18.3%; 45 randomized responders
rows.summary: 5-y OS 77.5% vs 31.2% (published HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.11–0.92); tumor-event-free survival 76.8% vs 18.3%; 45 randomized responders
rows.caution: Selected responders; closed early; published abstract corrects a discrepant draft; final full text unavailable
rows.shortCaution: Selected responders; closed early; published abstract corrects a discrepant draft; final full text unavailable
rows.author: Mazzaferro

rows.label: Sapisochin ITT
rows.population: SBRT vs TACE vs RFA bridge to LT (retrospective) · 36/99/244
rows.result: Waitlist drop-out 16.7% vs 20.2% vs 16.8% (P=0.7); ITT survival from listing at 5 years 61% vs 56% vs 61% (P=0.4)
rows.summary: Waitlist drop-out 16.7% vs 20.2% vs 16.8% (P=0.7); ITT survival from listing at 5 years 61% vs 56% vs 61% (P=0.4)
rows.caution: Retrospective; SBRT reserved for patients unfit for TACE/RFA; only 36 SBRT patients, underpowered
rows.shortCaution: Retrospective; SBRT reserved for patients unfit for TACE/RFA; only 36 SBRT patients, underpowered
rows.author: Sapisochin

rows.label: Mohamed 2016
rows.population: 60 recipients; 79 treatments across SBRT, TACE, RFA and Y90; only 9 Y90 and 9 RFA treatments.
rows.result: Complete pathologic response was reported in 75% after Y90 and 60% after RFA among evaluable explants.
rows.caution: Very small, unequal evaluable groups, mixed treatments and recipient selection; illustrative pathology results, not a modality ranking or dropout comparison.
rows.summary: Explant complete necrosis varied by modality in very small treatment groups.
rows.shortCaution: Recipient-only, nonrandomized and tiny denominators; no ranking of modalities or dropout effect.
rows.author: Mohamed

rows.label: Kwong 2022
rows.population: 31,609 US HCC transplant candidates, 2003–2018; 24,145 received LRT.
rows.result: IPTW-adjusted dropout sHR versus TACE: radioembolization 0.85 (95% CI 0.81–0.89); thermal ablation 0.95 (0.91–0.99).
rows.caution: Observational first-treatment comparison, with later treatments allowed. Center, era and patient selection remain confounders. Registry cohorts overlap with later studies.
rows.summary: IPTW dropout sHR vs TACE: Y90 0.85 (0.81–0.89); ablation 0.95 (0.91–0.99).
rows.shortCaution: Observational first-treatment comparison; overlapping registry cohorts and residual confounding.
rows.author: Kwong

rows.label: Yu 2026
rows.population: 53 transplanted patients; RS 28 versus TACE-MWA 25; 40 tumors per group, HCC ≤5 cm.
rows.result: Mean pathologic tumor necrosis 83.6% versus 79.0% (p=0.484); treatment modality was not independently associated with complete necrosis.
rows.caution: Transplanted patients only; cannot assess waitlist dropout. Complete-necrosis percentages have inconsistent denominators in Table 2 and are omitted. Most RS doses preceded current high-dose practice.
rows.summary: Mean tumor necrosis 83.6% vs 79.0% (p=0.484).
rows.shortCaution: Recipient-only; no dropout estimate. Full-text complete-necrosis denominators are inconsistent.
rows.author: Yu

rows.label: Lewandowski 2009
rows.population: UNOS T3 HCC; 43 TARE versus 43 TACE patients.
rows.result: Downstaging to T2: Y90 25/43 (58%) versus TACE 11/35 (31%), p=0.023. The 61% versus 37% figures describe partial response.
rows.caution: Retrospective. Eight TACE patients lacked follow-up imaging and were excluded from response analyses. Downstaging measured the whole lesion, including necrotic tissue; this is not the current viable-tumor method.
rows.summary: Downstaging to T2: 25/43 (58%) vs 11/35 (31%).
rows.shortCaution: Eight TACE cases lacked imaging. Whole-lesion sizing, not current viable-tumor criteria.
rows.author: Lewandowski

rows.label: Gabr 2017
rows.population: 172 transplanted patients: Y90 93 versus TACE 79.
rows.result: Post-LT recurrence 9% versus 8%; RFS and OS did not differ significantly.
rows.caution: Only recipients were analyzed. This cannot establish equivalent bridging success or compare dropout before transplantation.
rows.summary: Recurrence 9% vs 8%; no significant OS or recurrence-free survival difference.
rows.shortCaution: Recipients only; cannot estimate waitlist dropout or establish equivalence.
rows.author: Gabr

rows.label: MERITS-LT
rows.population: Prospective multicentre cohort · 209 UNOS-DS patients
rows.result: No significant Y90–TACE difference in downstaging; observational, not equivalence evidence
rows.summary: No significant Y90–TACE difference in downstaging; observational, not equivalence evidence
rows.caution: Post-LT follow-up median 1.7 y in 63 patients; TACE vs Y90 choice non-random, comparison unadjusted
rows.shortCaution: Post-LT follow-up median 1.7 y in 63 patients; TACE vs Y90 choice non-random, comparison unadjusted

rows.summary: Weighted cause-specific dropout HR 0.78 (0.69–0.89); 2-year dropout 14.2% vs 19.0%.

rows.population: 192 GEP-NET patients: cTACE 122, DEB-TACE 26, Y90 44.
rows.result: Propensity-weighted median OS: cTACE versus Y90 34.0 versus 22.9 months (p=0.032); cTACE versus DEB-TACE 33.8 versus 23.4 months (p=0.04).

rows.label: Currie 2020
rows.population: NELM patients surviving ≥1 year: TACE 63 versus TARE 28; chronic grade ≥3 hepatic toxicity beginning ≥6 months after treatment.
rows.result: Chronic hepatic toxicity: 22% versus 29%. Injury attributed solely to embolotherapy: 3% versus 14% (p=0.07), with more clinical decompensation after TARE.
rows.caution: Retrospective survivor-selected cohort. Most TACE toxicities coincided with progression. This cannot estimate toxicity in all treated patients or establish equivalent safety.
rows.summary: Chronic hepatic toxicity 22% vs 29%; solely embolotherapy-attributed injury 3% vs 14% (p=0.07).
rows.shortCaution: Selected survivors; many injuries coincided with progression. TARE more often caused decompensation.
rows.author: Currie
